lesson.menu_desc: How executives talk about differences -- comparatives and superlatives -- 25 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 6 -- Better, Worse, or the Same
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Mauricio | Lesson 6 -- Better, Worse, or the Same

listenings.text: Let me put the two years side by side, because the headline number is misleading. Last year we grew eight percent. This year we grew four. So on paper, this year is worse. But last year we grew by adding clients we should never have taken, and half of them are gone now. This year the growth is smaller, and it is entirely from clients we already had. Compared to last year, the number is worse and the business is better. My point is that the trend matters more than the number, and the most expensive mistake in my sector is to celebrate the wrong one.

I want to push back on that, politely. You said the American model is the most efficient, and by one measure it is. It is faster, and it is cheaper per transaction. But efficiency is not the only thing we are buying. Unlike the American model, the European one keeps the client relationship inside the bank, and that is worth something the spreadsheet does not show. So I would not say one is better than the other. I would say they are optimised for different things, and the trade-off is between speed and closeness. Whichever you pick, you are giving something up.

items.situation: Compare this year with last year at your desk, and say which is better and why.
tips: This year is ... than last year

items.situation: Somebody says your market cannot be compared to theirs. Disagree, politely.
tips: I would say the problem is the same.

items.situation: Describe the trade-off in your own strategy, in one sentence.
tips: We pay in ..., they pay in ...

items.situation: Ask two questions comparing the other person’s market to yours.
tips: What is the trade-off for you?

items.situation: You want to say something is not possible to keep doing for long. The word will not come.
tips: Sorry, how do you say this in English?
I mean something you cannot keep doing ...
it works now, but not for years ...
